## Second review of #68 (read-only; nothing flashed, committed or posted)

### What I ran
- Re-measured four clips with ONE fold-anchored script (`review2/remeasure.py`, same band/null statistic for all, auto- and hand-centred): default IMG_5864, sparse IMG_5866 (decoded fresh), speed 0.5 (`l5870.raw`), speed 0.3 (`e540.raw`). Results reproduce yours: band 0.854/0.947/0.937/0.971; whole-display 0.904/0.969/0.951/0.979; nulls 0.995–1.006.
- Dumped 81 consecutive host frames of the dense and sparse builds (index 52 in your `dump_*` binaries; the fake clock moves 1/30 s a frame, so each frame is ~0.4 px of scroll) and measured newly-lit fraction and luminance-weighted deficit against step size. Also dilated lines to test thickness.
- Read the hack, `main.cpp` probe diff, scripts, gl.md/gl-budget, issue thread.

### 1. Conclusions: supported, overstated, untested
**Supported (measurement):** pixel-local lag. Patches identical every push stay flat (0.998 = null) while 94%-relit strokes dip; a dark→grey toggle lags with a 2–5% tail. The magnitude also checks out from first principles: 29% of line light is lum>200 (A-type, 27% short at +1) and the rest B-type (9% short); 0.95 × (0.29×0.27 + 0.71×0.09) ≈ 13.5% versus your 12.6% band dip. Note a mechanism name: LTPS TFT hysteresis ("first-frame" luminance lag) is the standard AMOLED effect that fits this; panel makers fix it with driver-side overdrive LUTs we cannot reach.

**Overstated:** "scales with the fraction of lit pixels newly lit". From host sequences the newly-lit fraction at your device step sizes is 2.3 px→95%, 1.56 px (sparse)→84–88%, 1.17 px→64%, 0.7 px→43%. Measured whole-display dips (null-corrected): 11%, 3.8%, 6.3%, 2.5%. So (a) dense dip is super-linear in step size (~px^1.3), and (b) **the sparse build is an outlier**: at the same px/s and 1.56 px/push it dips 2.5× less than the dense build interpolated to that step. Same line thickness, same luminance mix (lum>200 share 0.29 both). The only differences are push rate (7.35 vs 4.9 Hz) and half the lines. Your model predicts ~15% for it; it shows 3.8%. This is unexplained and is the most important open row, because it says "more, smaller pushes" may buy more than linear relief.

**Wrong in the posted correction:** "TinyGL does no line smoothing, hard 2 px strokes". The patch draws Wu anti-aliased lines when `GL_LINE_SMOOTH` is on (gl.md:88, `tinygl_patch.py:110`); the dump has 108 grey levels and median line luminance 154. So most line pixels are grey (B-type transitions) and even sub-pixel motion changes levels — consistent with the near-static build not dipping only because 0.023 px/push is tiny.

**Untested:** CABC/ACL (agreed). Also a feature in every clip: a +1.7–1.8% bright frame two frames *before* the dip (default, sparse; +0.4% at 0.5). The settle window (+10..+20) also sits ~1.4% below the pre-push level, i.e. recovery has a >100 ms tail. Both are consistent with hysteresis, but check the pre-pulse on a static push (toggle clip) to rule out encoder/rolling-shutter artefact. Sparse "5.7%" came from a threshold-selected event picker (analyse4, events only where whole<0.985) while the sweep used fold anchoring; my common script gives 5.1% band, so the two were comparable after all.

**By-eye rows:** unblinded, one observer, builds known; the 6.2%-visible vs 5.7%-invisible comparison is within method noise (I get 6.3% vs 5.1% band) and differs in rate, so it cannot separate depth from rate.

### 2. Best explanation
Panel pixel lag (TFT hysteresis) remains the best single explanation; nothing global survives the patch control. But it does not predict the sparse row or the super-linearity, so state it as "local lag, with an unexplained rate/density dependence".

### 3. Overdrive probe
Not a fair test, for a reason not in the record: RGB565 headroom. On the real line pixels a 120% gain gives a luminance-weighted boost of only 1.136; 27% of line light gets <10% and 8% of lit pixels (0xFFFF) get nothing — and those are the A-type pixels that lag most. Also the plain clips already show a pre-dip bright frame, so the "+2–6% pulse" is not all overdrive. And the restore push lands 12–30 ms later, which likely *is* the dip you saw (a second transition). A fairer design: render the scene at 80% brightness so every pixel has headroom, boost newly-lit pixels to 100% for one push and restore in the *next regular push* (no extra push, no rate loss). Worth one flash only because it is cheap; expect partial relief at best.

### 4. Is `*speed: 0.3` the right stop?
It is a safe mitigation but not the best lever. Ranked:
1. **Raise the push rate at the same px/s** — the sparse row suggests 7 Hz halves the dip beyond the step-size effect. Levers: `glshim_set_render_scale(2)` (half-res exists; also doubles effective line thickness → newly-lit at 2 px step falls 84%→54% by dilation test), or `*resolution: 50` with 40 rows. Needs a flash + film; host dumps can preview thickness only.
2. **Thicker lines** (shim honours `glLineWidth`, or draw the strip twice offset 1 px): 84%→54%→40% newly lit for +1/+2 px. Host-testable now; look changes.
3. **Speed 0.3** (2.5% whole): known, invisible, but "slow".

## Second review of #68 (read-only; nothing flashed, committed or posted)

### What I ran
- Re-measured four clips with ONE fold-anchored script (`review2/remeasure.py`, same band/null statistic for all, auto- and hand-centred): default IMG_5864, sparse IMG_5866 (decoded fresh), speed 0.5 (`l5870.raw`), speed 0.3 (`e540.raw`). Results reproduce yours: band 0.854/0.947/0.937/0.971; whole-display 0.904/0.969/0.951/0.979; nulls 0.995–1.006.
- Dumped 81 consecutive host frames of the dense and sparse builds (index 52 in your `dump_*` binaries; the fake clock moves 1/30 s a frame, so each frame is ~0.4 px of scroll) and measured newly-lit fraction and luminance-weighted deficit against step size. Also dilated lines to test thickness.
- Read the hack, `main.cpp` probe diff, scripts, gl.md/gl-budget, issue thread.

### 1. Conclusions: supported, overstated, untested
**Supported (measurement):** pixel-local lag. Patches identical every push stay flat (0.998 = null) while 94%-relit strokes dip; a dark→grey toggle lags with a 2–5% tail. The magnitude also checks out from first principles: 29% of line light is lum>200 (A-type, 27% short at +1) and the rest B-type (9% short); 0.95 × (0.29×0.27 + 0.71×0.09) ≈ 13.5% versus your 12.6% band dip. Note a mechanism name: LTPS TFT hysteresis ("first-frame" luminance lag) is the standard AMOLED effect that fits this; panel makers fix it with driver-side overdrive LUTs we cannot reach.

**Overstated:** "scales with the fraction of lit pixels newly lit". From host sequences the newly-lit fraction at your device step sizes is 2.3 px→95%, 1.56 px (sparse)→84–88%, 1.17 px→64%, 0.7 px→43%. Measured whole-display dips (null-corrected): 11%, 3.8%, 6.3%, 2.5%. So (a) dense dip is super-linear in step size (~px^1.3), and (b) **the sparse build is an outlier**: at the same px/s and 1.56 px/push it dips 2.5× less than the dense build interpolated to that step. Same line thickness, same luminance mix (lum>200 share 0.29 both). The only differences are push rate (7.35 vs 4.9 Hz) and half the lines. Your model predicts ~15% for it; it shows 3.8%. This is unexplained and is the most important open row, because it says "more, smaller pushes" may buy more than linear relief.

**Wrong in the posted correction:** "TinyGL does no line smoothing, hard 2 px strokes". The patch draws Wu anti-aliased lines when `GL_LINE_SMOOTH` is on (gl.md:88, `tinygl_patch.py:110`); the dump has 108 grey levels and median line luminance 154. So most line pixels are grey (B-type transitions) and even sub-pixel motion changes levels — consistent with the near-static build not dipping only because 0.023 px/push is tiny.

**Untested:** CABC/ACL (agreed). Also a feature in every clip: a +1.7–1.8% bright frame two frames *before* the dip (default, sparse; +0.4% at 0.5). The settle window (+10..+20) also sits ~1.4% below the pre-push level, i.e. recovery has a >100 ms tail. Both are consistent with hysteresis, but check the pre-pulse on a static push (toggle clip) to rule out encoder/rolling-shutter artefact. Sparse "5.7%" came from a threshold-selected event picker (analyse4, events only where whole<0.985) while the sweep used fold anchoring; my common script gives 5.1% band, so the two were comparable after all.

**By-eye rows:** unblinded, one observer, builds known; the 6.2%-visible vs 5.7%-invisible comparison is within method noise (I get 6.3% vs 5.1% band) and differs in rate, so it cannot separate depth from rate.

### 2. Best explanation
Panel pixel lag (TFT hysteresis) remains the best single explanation; nothing global survives the patch control. But it does not predict the sparse row or the super-linearity, so state it as "local lag, with an unexplained rate/density dependence".

### 3. Overdrive probe
Not a fair test, for a reason not in the record: RGB565 headroom. On the real line pixels a 120% gain gives a luminance-weighted boost of only 1.136; 27% of line light gets <10% and 8% of lit pixels (0xFFFF) get nothing — and those are the A-type pixels that lag most. Also the plain clips already show a pre-dip bright frame, so the "+2–6% pulse" is not all overdrive. And the restore push lands 12–30 ms later, which likely *is* the dip you saw (a second transition). A fairer design: render the scene at 80% brightness so every pixel has headroom, boost newly-lit pixels to 100% for one push and restore in the *next regular push* (no extra push, no rate loss). Worth one flash only because it is cheap; expect partial relief at best.

### 4. Is `*speed: 0.3` the right stop?
It is a safe mitigation but not the best lever. Ranked:
1. **Raise the push rate at the same px/s** — the sparse row suggests 7 Hz halves the dip beyond the step-size effect. Levers: `glshim_set_render_scale(2)` (half-res exists; also doubles effective line thickness → newly-lit at 2 px step falls 84%→54% by dilation test), or `*resolution: 50` with 40 rows. Needs a flash + film; host dumps can preview thickness only.
2. **Thicker lines** (shim honours `glLineWidth`, or draw the strip twice offset 1 px): 84%→54%→40% newly lit for +1/+2 px. Host-testable now; look changes.
3. **Speed 0.3** (2.5% whole): known, invisible, but "slow".
4. Darker background pedestal (e.g. 0x2104) to avoid black→bright: B-type transitions lag less at +1 (0.91 vs 0.73). Untested; look changes.
5. Reduced-brightness lines/colour: no reason to expect a relative change.
